title: August issue — check what stuck
intro: Eight self-check questions from the August 2026 Wealth Insight.

choices: Nvidia has the lower P/E and far faster growth — yet Coke outperformed this year, because kind, durability and priced-in matter more than rate
questions.explanation: 'This is not how markets work' — the multiple encodes a durability judgement. Hot, capital-attracting cycles get their growth re-priced; predictable compounding earns a premium.

choices: Depreciation from ~₹1,700 crore of expansion capex crushing EPS — EV/EBITDA reads the operations honestly, though the 12% ROCE is a real concern
A perfect business worth any price
questions.explanation: Match the multiple to the business: P/E breaks on capex-heavy expansion. But the lens-switch must not bury the honest weakness — capital that hasn't yet earned its keep.

questions.prompt: Bank of Baroda at 0.9× book illustrates…
choices: That cheap banks are always broken
'Poor form has a long afterlife' — the discount persists on remembered sins even as RoA exceeds 1% and RoE reaches mid-teens
That book value doesn't apply to banks
questions.explanation: Banks are read through book value + returns on it — and the afterlife of poor form is where that lens finds its bargains.

questions.prompt: Castrol India's flat decade despite 40%+ return on capital teaches…
choices: Quality without growth persists but doesn't compound — a matured market and the EV ceiling capped the future
questions.explanation: The compromise audit: remove growth and even an exceptional business just persists. (HDFC Bank teaches the valuation leg: a near-perfect record can't rescue the entry price.)

questions.prompt: A dividend's special information value is that…
choices: Profits can be presented favorably, but sustained cash out the door cannot — dividends tell what income statements often don't
questions.explanation: The dividend-honesty framework — with its twin question: is this payout strength, or a business that has stopped reinvesting?

questions.prompt: The four-bottoms study found that from ordinary correction bottoms (2009/2012/2013/2016)…
choices: Roughly one listed company in ten cleared the outlier hurdle — while 2020's panic prices lifted it to about one in three
questions.explanation: A steady 1-in-10 crop from ordinary corrections; the 2020 anomaly came from the entry discount — the bounce alone packed years of return into quarters. And the winners table stays survivorship-biased throughout.

questions.prompt: The Desi Retirement Plan's central corrective is…
choices: A universal corpus number for every retiree
India teaches accumulation, not decumulation — retirement is a life stage where money must be split by job, with healthcare the wildcard
questions.explanation: 'Will your money outlive you, or will you outlive your money?' One pool of money cannot do every job at once.

choices: About 5.5% a year — a quiet lifetime leak most rupee-only portfolios never price
Nothing — exchange rates don't affect investors
questions.explanation: (96/9)^(1/44) − 1 ≈ 5.5%/yr. The hedge hiding in plain sight: hard-currency-linked earning power inside the portfolio.
